title: Epoched ingest normalizer to resolve time-travel counts in Console per-model charts
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: Console per-model charts sometimes show a transient negative dip or sudden spike when delayed usage events are backfilled. Root cause analysis found that late events with event_time < current_bucket but ingest_time in a later processing epoch are being naively applied to existing aggregates, which can cause compaction and correction logic to produce temporary negative values or duplicate attribution across shards.

Problem details:
- We rely on two timestamps: event_time (when token/usage originated) and ingest_time (when the event was processed by the pipeline).
- When backfills arrive, our timeseries compaction reconciler applies corrections in the ingest epoch order. If a late event maps to an earlier event_time bucket but is reconciled after a summary compaction, the existing aggregated delta is adjusted by subtracting an older provisional value and adding the new one, but race conditions and out-of-order shard merges produce intermediate negative dips.
- This is especially visible for per-model breakdowns (small buckets) and for customers with multi-region sharded ingestion where shard clocks and epoch boundaries differ.

Why this matters:
- Customer-facing Console charts show confusing negative dips and short-lived spikes that trigger alerts and support tickets.
- Billing and quota UI can temporarily present incorrect top-N model lists and per-route cost estimates.
- Current mitigations (UI smoothing, longer smoothing windows) hide symptoms but do not address correctness and make latency of corrections worse.

Proposed solution: Epoched ingest normalizer
- Add an explicit ingest_epoch tag to aggregated intermediate summaries and to the reconciliation protocol. Each timeseries bucket will maintain a small vector of recent epoch deltas (bounded length, e.g., last 4 epochs) rather than a single mutable counter.
- On late-epoch arrival, instead of mutating the single counter in place, write the delta into the epoch slot for its event_time bucket. During compaction, merge rules will perform stable monotonic reconciliation: final_count = base + sum(epoch_slots). Removal or correction of earlier provisional writes will mark the slot as corrected rather than subtracting directly from final_count, avoiding transient negative intermediate values.
- Implement a background compaction pass that collapses old epoch slots (older than retention threshold) into the base value atomically.

Implementation notes and constraints: 
- Storage: augment bucket proto with small fixed-size array and a metadata epoch index. Keep serialization compact to avoid doubling storage for high-cardinality indexes.
- Read path: presentation layer must sum base + epoch_slots when rendering charts. Provide a compatibility mode that falls back to current single-counter buckets for older clusters during rollout.
- Backfill runner: adjust backfill job to set ingest_epoch based on the backfill run id, enabling future attribution and targeted corrections.
- Availability: design to be resilient to partial deploys; early reads should not show inconsistency when only some components are updated. Use feature flags and read-side compatibility.

Rollout plan: 
1) Design review + proto change (1 week).
2) Implement storage + reconciliation in data pipeline (2 weeks).
3) Add read-path summation in Console and a hidden feature-flagged rollout (1 week).
4) Run staged backfill of historical late events in Canary region and monitor charts for disappearance of negative dips (1 week).
5) Expand to global; run compaction to collapse old epochs after 30 days of stable operation.

Monitoring and KPIs: 
- Metric: rate of negative-value transient events per 24h on per-model timeseries (target: reduce to zero for new data).
- Metric: number of support tickets referencing "negative" or "unexpected dip" (target: -80% within 2 weeks of rollout).
- Dashboards: add a reconciliation health dashboard showing epoch slot occupancy, compaction lag, and per-shard correction counts.

Risks and trade-offs: 
- Slightly higher storage and CPU for read-time summation. We'll mitigate via fixed-size slots and compaction.
- Complexity during cross-cluster rollout could produce mixed views; mitigated via feature flags and a compatibility read-mode.
- Edge-case: very-high-cardinality models could increase memory pressure; add sampling and eviction policies for zero-valued epoch slots.
acceptance_criteria: Per-model Console charts no longer show transient negative dips caused by late-event reconciliation for canary dataset (observed over 72h)
Backfill job writes ingest_epoch and new aggregated buckets reflect epoch-slot usage in storage layer confirmed by data audits
No regression in total tokens counted for billing when compared with golden dataset (within 0.1%)
Feature-flag remote toggle works: enabling/disabling new read-path yields consistent charts without crashes
Compaction job successfully collapses epochs older than configured threshold and reclaimed storage is within forecast
comments: 2025-01-12 - Investigated root cause with infra: reprobed pipeline with synthetic late events. Confirmed negative dips when shard merge order differs from event_time ordering.
2025-01-16 - Design doc drafted: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/epoched-ingest-normalizer (internal) - awaiting review from data-platform and console teams.
2025-01-22 - Sync with Console: read-path summation will be hidden behind feature flag `epoched_read_v1`. Console required an opt-in rollout window.
2025-01-28 - Prototype implemented in staging: storage proto extended with 4 epoch slots. Unit tests added for merge semantics.
2025-02-03 - Canary backfill run started for customers A,B,C in us-west1; monitoring panel created: https://grafana.redwood/board/reconciliation-epoched
2025-02-05 - Early canary results: negative-dip incidents reduced by 92% in the canary cohort. Observed small increase in read CPU; engineering will add an optimized summation path next sprint.
